# arunodhayan's original training driver — vendored verbatim, not ours

`train.py` (1138 lines) is arunodhayan's own script for his 3rd-place solution — verified
directly (not assumed) to be his *original* recipe: its active `CUSTOM_TRAINER =
"nnUNetTrainer_RotFlip_ClDice_prob0.8_arun"` and the DC+CE+clDice/RAdamScheduleFree recipe
match exactly what `docs/attribution.md` independently cites this file for elsewhere
(replicated as `nnUNetTrainerSeeded_ClDice_ScheduleFree` for the Phase 3, item 11 ablation).
It produced the **zero-shot checkpoint** (Phase 2, item 8) that Phase 3 item 12's fine-tune
started from — it is cited/vendored here as the provenance record for that checkpoint, the
same role `docs/checkpoints.md` gives m7's and STU-Net's public checkpoints.

**It is *not* the script that produced item 12's fine-tuned checkpoint.** Grepped directly for
"highpass"/"skeleton"/"affinity" in this file: zero matches. Item 12's actual training code
(the highpass input + skeleton-recall + affinity combination, hand-adapted for that one run)
is not present in this file, anywhere else in this repo, or in the old `finetune/` working
directory it was vendored from — it appears to be genuinely lost, not merely uncommitted. This
correction was made after the user asked, directly, why item 12 was marked non-reproducible;
re-reading this file's own content to check the claim (rather than trusting what a prior pass
of this documentation asserted) is what surfaced the mislabeling. See
`docs/reproducibility_notes.md` item 1 for the corrected, full account.

It is vendored here **unmodified**, exactly as it produced the zero-shot checkpoint, because
this is what actually happened — not a reconstruction of what should have happened.

**This is not our code.** It's arunodhayan's own training driver, exactly as he ran it for his
3rd-place solution. See `docs/attribution.md` for the full source citation.

## What it actually is, plainly

- A single, monolithic, notebook-derived script: `os.environ["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"] = "0,1"`
  set at import time, several absolute/dataset-name-baked-in paths
  (`19feb_vesuvius-surface-nnunet-preprocessed_prob0.8`, `19feb_nnUNet_data_...`), and a bare
  `full_pipeline(epochs=8000)` call at the very bottom of the file — running the script *is*
  the invocation, there's no CLI or `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard.
- `finetune_cascade.yaml.orig` sat in the same directory during the real run but **was never
  read by `train.py`** — the association between the two files is historical (they lived side
  by side), not functional. Don't assume the yaml's settings describe what actually happened;
  the hardcoded values inside `train.py` itself are the only real record.
- Do not edit this file. If you want a readable, config-driven starting point for fine-tuning
  arunodhayan's checkpoint via nnU-Net's standard `-pretrained_weights` mechanism, see
  `src/vesuvius_surface/training/finetune/arunodhayan_cascade_driver.py` — a generic driver
  written from how nnU-Net transfer learning works, not extracted from this script (this
  script doesn't contain item 12's fine-tune logic — see above). It does not reproduce item
  12's specific highpass+skeleton-recall+affinity recipe, since that recipe's own source no
  longer exists to extract from. See `docs/reproducibility_notes.md` item 1 for the full,
  honest gap this represents.
